sign_test.interpretation: 8/9 models show positive indirect effect; binomial sign test p=0.0195 (one-sided)

wilcoxon_test.statistic_method: Wilcoxon signed-rank on per-model indirect effects
wilcoxon_test.caveat: Treats models as independent; they share classes, so this is anti-conservative.

t_test.statistic_method: One-sample t-test on per-model indirect effects (H0: mean<=0)
t_test.caveat: Treats models as independent; they share classes, so this is anti-conservative.

pooled_mean_indirect.interpretation: Cross-model mean indirect effect = +0.536, 95% CI [-0.515, +0.888], p=0.0886 (one-sided H0: mean<=0)

method: Cluster bootstrap: resample 13 classes with replacement (seed 20260801, 10000 replicates); for each resample compute the indirect effect for each of the 9 models and average. The class is the cluster unit, preserving the cross-model dependency on the same classes. Sign test is binomial under H0: sign is a fair coin.
conclusion: Although each model's individual CI on n=13 classes spans zero, the cross-model agreement is significant: 8/9 models show positive indirect effects (sign test p=0.0195), and the pooled mean indirect effect = +0.536 with 95% CI [-0.515, +0.888] (includes zero). This indicates a consistent positive indirect effect across models that the individual (underpowered) CIs fail to resolve.
